questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a big and interesting city, and I wanted the university to have a great reputation. For me UCL was perfect in both aspects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult. I wish I had known had hard and frustating it would be. However, it was all worth it when I arrived and figured it all out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was "Welcome-days" and opportunities to ask for help for anything like enrolment and choosing classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult, as the housing market in London is a bit chaotic. Everything is expensive, because so many people want to live in the city, close to city center. It was stressful at first, but as soon as you figure something out, there are no more problems and you can just enjoy your time there. It felt overwhelming, but it is for a short period of time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend it. Some people got to meet new people and make friends at their student accomedations, but to me it seemed that for the most part, people just stayed in their rooms and didn't do that much socialising.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We didn't get offered any student housing

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There were plenty of information about the classes available, but the system was very stupid. The have a program for you to write in classes and see it there are any clashes, however it is very amnual and took so long. You just have to try out so many combinations until you find something.
Then you had to write to your coordinator that you wanted a certain class, and to the module organizer, asking if you could take that module, and they both had to accept that. And then you do that for four modules, ad if there is a problem, you start over with a new class and see if it clashes. Very annoying.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Your coordinators will do a lot to help you, you just write whatever questions you have by email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted, even though all of them weren't exactly what I had hoped.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry to much about choosing from home, you will have to change everything when you get there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the classes was a bit easier than at KU, at least a lot less preparations and readings to do before lectures

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller classes, less formal (even though you call everyone "Dr." or "professor"), I liked it a lot.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Infection
Receptor Mechanisms
Introduction to Coding for Bioscience Research (python)
Social Neurosciende of Model Animals

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved my coding class and infection (even though infection was 100% online). I would recommend both a lot!

questions.answer: We ate out and went out more than I had thought, but it was worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is cheaper than in Denmark, underground was expensive however necessary

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had more than 300 different clubs to join, everything for "boba-lovers" and movie societies over culture or nationality societies to innovation or economy clubs. And societies just about any sport

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the nordic society, the food market every thursday and the welcome-activities for international students, which is where I met most of my friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Sky garden
The street food markets of London, like Camden food market, borough market, international food market on brick lane, the food market in hackney every weekend, Seven Dials market
Go to columbia street flower market!!
Protobello road market, they have street food as well
Try as many restaurants as you can, that is how the locals live
Walking in regents park, that was my favourite
Walk around Covent garden
Se the view from Hampstead Heath
Visit the fampus museums, they are free. Try Tate Modern, natural history and british museum
Try afternoon tea!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Very easy
Get a pret membership, then you fit right in

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to then in class, people take different classes and often don't already know each other. Your not the only new face and they are not all friends already

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Eating out

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare yourself for a difficult beginning, the communication with UCL is awful and finding housing is stressful (but all worth it after the first week when everything is in order)

Go to the "welcome-events" the few days and talk to people in your classes

Enjoy yourself, the culture is very similar and it doesn't take that much work to get used to it. So just relax and enjoy being in a great city that has something new to offer everyday

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress to much before arriving, you'll get it sorted out there

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Figuring out the difficult situation with housing myself. Meeting new friends and people from all over the world. Improving my english. Getting to know and love London, actually that is number one, it was the best.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: finding housing and everything before I arrived

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
